I'd estimate a modest positive effect on multidimensional trust, somewhere around 1.3-1.8 points.

Working through the other secondary measures, I'm penciling in small increases across trust, distrust reduction, funding perceptions, and institutional trust, with even smaller effects on concern, policy support, behavior, and donation intentions — since the text focuses purely on measurement methodology rather than climate impacts or policy advocacy.

Since this variant is "Measurement & modeling (2)," likely a related but slightly more jargon-heavy version of the intervention, I'll set its effects a touch weaker than a first version, settling trust around 1.4 and finalizing everything with realistic non-round values.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary:
This arm is a dry, expository, jargon-heavy description of climate-science methodology (instruments, statistical models, reproducibility). Its mechanism is almost purely epistemic-competence signaling: it should raise perceptions that climate scientists are rigorous, methodical, and data-driven rather than subjective, which is exactly the competence (and partly integrity) subscale of the primary multidimensional trust battery. Because it is didactic rather than narrative, contains no messenger congruence, no counter-attitudinal correction, and no risk/impact content, I expect a below-average-to-average trust effect (~1.3 points on the primary outcome) rather than the 2.5
cr3-point range reserved for source-credibility or debunking arms, and even less on the pre-anchored single-item trust and belief measures. Downstream outcomes are weakly connected: funding, institutional trust, belief, concern, and policy support get only trust-mediated spillover under ~0.6 points; policy_role is nearly flat because the text's emphasis on objectivity over "subjective impressions" cuts against advocacy endorsement while general trust pushes it up. Incentivized behaviors get near-zero effects, with a token positive for the AMS donation (a measurement/meteorology-adjacent recipient) and a fraction of a percentage point on newsletter sign-up.
